content.comment_body: Hello everyone, Can someone explain how retentivity works in the [product_name]? Does it use a built-in battery for this? I know that typical PLCs have batteries to retain programs and memory tags, but what is the solution for [product_name]?
The [product_name] saves retentivity data in flash memory, just like it does with the program.
Does this module have a battery?
No, earlier versions of the [product_name] used a battery.
An ultra capacitor, rated at 5.5 Volt 0.33UF, is used to maintain the real-time clock.

analysis.insight_summary: Participants are clarifying how retentivity data is managed in [product_name] modules, with a particular focus on the presence of a built-in battery. The responses confirm that the module relies on flash memory for data retention and does not require a battery for that purpose. Instead, an ultra capacitor keeps the real-time clock running. There is also historical mention that older units did rely on batteries.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect [product_name] modules to reliably retain data like traditional PLCs, and want clear details about whether a built-in battery is required for this functionality.
